title: cost-opt-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Motivation: customers repeatedly ask for production-safe defaults and automated recommendations that reduce per-token costs without regressing quality. This PR introduces a coordinated stack of features: (1) autotune controller for batching and KV/prefix caching defaults driven by incoming traffic profiles, (2) quantization profile registry and recommendation engine that suggests safe quant levels per model archetype + workload, and (3) unit-economics (UEcon) tooling to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs and produce actionable rollout configs. Changes are conservative by default (recommendations are opt-in) and include telemetry to validate quality regressions. Checklist: - [x] Autotune controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Quant profiles registry + model compatibility matrix - [x] UEcon CLI and dashboard instrumentation - [x] End-to-end integration tests against perf-canary harness - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Feature flag gating for rollout

What this PR does (summary): - Adds pkg/autotune: controller that observes request size/arrival distributions and emits recommended defaults for batch_size, batch_window_ms, kv_cache_enabled, and prefix_cache_ttl. The controller exposes an evaluation endpoint used by the Console to preview suggested defaults. - Adds pkg/quantprofiles: a registry of quantization profiles (8-bit, 4-bit symmetric, GPTQ presets) with per-architecture safety metadata and expected memory/speed savings. Includes a lightweight simulator to estimate quality impact using cached evals. - Adds cmd/uecon: a CLI to run unit-econ simulations (cost-per-1M-tokens, p95 latency, throughput) given a workload trace and candidate config set. CLI outputs CSV/JSON that the Console consumes. - Console + docs: new Optimize -> Autotune page that surfaces recommendations, estimated savings, and quick-apply with canary rollout templates. - CI and perf harness: integration tests added to infra/ci and a perf-canary job to validate tail-latency regressions under recommended configs.

Testing & results: - CI: unit + integration + e2e pass after addressing a flaky race in the controller (fixed by adding a backoff retry). - Perf: on internal canary traces we saw median cost per token reduction of ~17% and 95th percentile latency change of +1.9% (within SLO). - Safety: quantization simulator flagged potential >2% generation-quality regressions for one LLaMA-variant; that profile is gated and requires manual opt-in.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.autotune.enable; Console preview for account admins; default suggestions are opt-in per-model. We will run a 2-week canary on internal traffic then enable gradual rollout to customers who opt into "cost-savings beta". Follow-ups: automatic A/B evaluation hooks to measure quality regressions and integration with rollback policies.

review_comments: Aisha Khan: Left a couple of nits on the controller API (prefer explicit time.Duration parsing) and asked for a defensive nil-check when loading saved traces.
Jordan Lee (author): Addressed nits, added parsing helpers and explicit error messages. PTAL.
Miguel Torres: Concern about automatic application of quant profiles to production model variants. Suggested opt-in and an internal audit log. Added a request for a canary-run template.
Jordan Lee: Quant application is opt-in by default and audit events are emitted (pkg/observability/events_autotune.go). Added canary template to examples/quickstart-autotune.yaml.
Priya Desai: Verified UEcon CLI outputs match Console ingestion format. Asked for example CSV in docs. Added example and unit tests for CLI formatter.
release_notes: Adds an autotune controller that recommends batching/caching defaults, a quantization profile registry with a safety-first simulator, and unit-economics tooling (CLI + Console preview). Recommendations are opt-in and feature-gated. Expected impact: up to ~20% cost-per-token reduction for compatible workloads with minimal latency regression. See docs/optimize/autotune.md for migration and canary instructions.
